$comment: PLAN rule 14 as a number. A layer nothing else uses has never been proven to fit the stack — the split into nine packages is only real if the packages actually compose. `edges` is the count of dependency edges inside the family and it may only go up, the same ratchet the compat rates use. `awaiting` names the packages that have no consumer yet; a package must leave the list the moment it gains one, and the list may only shrink. `burgee` is never on it: it is the top of the stack, and nothing using it is correct.
target: every package except burgee is used by at least one other package in the family

why.bellpull: exists now — cross-spawn 68/68, up from a seven-line stub — but nothing imports it yet. `burgee/commander` still spawns with raw `node:child_process` and needs a `spawn()` that returns the ChildProcess; `compat-oracle/run.ts` needs `maxBuffer` and a sync call. Both are named in bellpull's design.md.
why.caique: 0 of 606 clack cases; burgee reaching it needs the guarded optional-surface mechanism U13 describes, which does not exist yet.
why.flagstaff: burgee renders no spinner, box or table anywhere; `weight.test.ts` denies it by name. The honest edge does not exist yet, and manufacturing one would defeat this ratchet.

$bellpull: bellpull left `awaiting` on 2026-09-17: `burgee/commander` spawns its `executableSubcommand` through `bellpull/cross-spawn`. The entry had sat in `inline-implementation-lock`'s KNOWN table with the condition written into it — "the engine lane adopts it once bellpull grades against cross-spawn's suite" — and bellpull grades 68 / 68. commander stayed 1360 / 1360 through the change. burgee no longer imports `node:child_process` at all; `ChildProcess` comes from bellpull, which re-exports it for exactly this consumer.
